guitar.notes: Original entry already well-balanced; keeping as-is — Petty/Campbell's gear genuinely spans multiple iconic instruments without one being singularly dominant.

tone.summary: A classic jangly rock tone achieved using a low-gain preamp (US Deluxe) combined with the AC30 model for brightness, slight compression, and minimal modulation.
gearClues: Vox AC30 or bright Fender combo

rig.name: Tom Petty - American Girl - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide light grit and boost the attack for jangly chords.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used to simulate a clean, slightly broken-up Fender/Vox edge without heavy distortion.

blocks.purpose: Keep distortion off to maintain clarity and jangle.
blocks.gap: No dedicated low-gain dirt pedal is needed; the Green OD handles the breakup.

blocks.purpose: Emulate the bright, chimey sound of a Vox AC30.
Provide a classic British cabinet sound that complements the AC30 tone.
blocks.gap: While 1x12 is preferred, the UK Vintage 4x12 offers enough brightness and clarity to mimic the desired Vox/Fender edge.

blocks.purpose: Enhance the upper mids and treble for maximum jangle and brightness.
Keep the tone open and jangly; no wah needed.
Avoid chorus as per the musical verdict.
blocks.gap: The Chorus module is bypassed to meet the 'avoid' criteria.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle depth and space without muddying the jangly attack.
blocks.gap: Used sparingly to enhance the open-chord feel, keeping it subtle.

blocks.purpose: Provide a natural, open room ambiance without sounding overly wet.

improvements.summary: Swap the current UK 4x12 cabinet for a smaller, brighter 1x12 or 2x12 to better match the desired Vox/Fender jangly tone.

proposals.reason: A smaller, brighter cabinet better captures the desired Vox/Fender chime and jangly attack.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased clarity and brightness in upper mids.
